newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures mixed, yen edges higher.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures mixed, yen edges higher.

text.p: April 16 - IMM currency futures still mixed. Yen firmed to day's high after US Trade Rep Barshefsky said concerned by trade imbalance with Japan. June yen cleared overnight peak at $0.008026 but stalled below key resistance at $0.008039. Yen firmed overnight when MoF's Sakakibara reiterated that yen moves excessive, said Japan will intervene when can "win."
Subsequent U.S. economic data that proved stronger than forecast shoved most units back to small losses and tugged June yen away from that resistance area as well.
March U.S. capacity use rose to a 84.1-percent rate, its highest level since March 1995. Industrial output rose 0.9 percent, the biggest one-month gain since April 1996.
Both March figures exceeded forecasts and suggested to some analysts that the U.S. economy is moving ahead at a fast enough clip to keep the Federal Reserve on inflation alert.
Sterling fell overseas after downwardly revised U.K. wages figures that helped allay concerns about a tight work force.
Some traders wait to see whether U.S. deputy Treasury secretary Lawrence Summers makes any market-moving remarks when he appears before the Senate Finance Committee starting at 0900 CDT/1400 GMT.

At 0846 CDT/1346 GMT, June yen rose $0.0026 to $0.008031, marks firmed $0.0003 to $0.5822, Swiss francs slipped $0.0006 to $0.6866, sterling declined $0.0072 to $1.6200, Canadian dollar dipped $0.0005 to $0.7181, Australian dollar fell $0.0029 to $0.7710, Mexican peso eased $0.000050 to $0.122725.
